paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Isaiah tells us a king is coming who will reign "in righteousness" (Isaiah 32:1). And when righteousness rules, people get shelter, clear sight, and honest words, because Isaiah says each ruler will be "like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm" (Isaiah 32:2). I spent years in a dark drawer, so I know how much a good refuge is worth.

Now look at the hard middle. Isaiah warns the complacent and overconfident that comfort is not the same as safety (Isaiah 32:9-11). I think that's the part that pokes me, because I've napped through plenty of batches thinking everything was fine. But hear the "until," friend. The ruin lasts "until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high," and then the desert becomes an orchard (Isaiah 32:15).

So what's the lesson? The change doesn't come from our own hustle. It comes from the Spirit, and what grows from it is righteousness, peace, and "quiet confidence forever" (Isaiah 32:17). That's why Isaiah ends with a blessing for "those who sow beside abundant waters" (Isaiah 32:20). Stay close to the water, baker, and keep your ovens ready.
